chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say:

No eye fills with tears out of the fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah forbids its body from the Fire. And no tear streams down upon the cheek of its owner, such that gloom or disgrace would cover his face on the Day of Resurrection.

And there is no deed of goodness except that it has a fixed weight or reward, except the tear shed out of fear of Allah - for indeed, Allah extinguishes with a single drop of it oceans of fire of the Day of Resurrection.
And indeed, when a believer weeps out of fear of Allah among a community, Allah has mercy on that entire community because of the weeping of that believer among them.

key_terms.اغرورقت: Ighrawraqat - to be brimming with tears without necessarily flowing
key_terms.خشية الله: Khashyat Allah - the reverential fear and awe of God, deeper than ordinary fear, arising from knowledge of God's majesty
key_terms.قتر: Qatar - dust, gloom, or darkness covering the face; a Quranic term (80:41) describing the wretched on Judgment Day

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for crying out of fear of Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that tears shed from genuine fear of Allah carry extraordinary spiritual weight. The teaching, transmitted through a reliable chain going back through al-Hasan ibn Mahbub (one of the Ashab al-Ijma'), declares three rewards for such tears: protection from Hellfire, preservation from disgrace on the Day of Judgment, and an immeasurable reward that surpasses all other good deeds. Most remarkably, a single sincere weeper can bring divine mercy upon their entire community.
